subject: Mid-quarter steering: strategy trim, rapid deps & QBR artifacts
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Park <sarah@nimbleai.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Mid-quarter steering: strategy trim, rapid deps & QBR artifacts

Team —

Quick mid-quarter check. Deck deadlines for the QBR are looming and I want to align on two things so we can lock the ask list for partners and infra by EOD Wednesday: 

1) Scope trims: proposal below to narrow deliverables for the quarter so the reliability and cost-effort initiatives land without overcommit.
   - Keep: model routing + cache-first rollout (MVP)
   - Defer: full multi-variant quantization plan (move to next quarter)
   - Reduce: experimental reranker to scoped evaluation (POC only)

2) Dependencies: I need explicit owner commitments for the infra items we must have in place for the hosted-to-dedicated routing test and the QBR demo. Namely:
   - KV cache retention policy changes (infra)
   - Canary routing rule for fallback to low-cost variant (serving/runtime)
   - Permissions & audit logs for the partner demo (security/compliance)

Action items I propose now (please confirm by replying):
- Vanessa: confirm which infra tickets you can unblock this sprint and which need escalation.
- Markus: confirm if a reduced scope still protects our latency SLOs for the demo. If not, propose alternatives.
- Naomi: approve the communication to NimbusCloud and partners with the revised scope and ask list.

Attached: QBR_onepager_v2.pdf (draft). I also added a short runbook stub for the demo run under attachments.

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Head of Product, Serving
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: partners@cloudmarket.com
Date: 2026-11-30T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter steering: strategy trim, rapid deps & QBR artifacts

Soojin —

Thanks for the clear asks. Quick status from infra: 

- KV cache retention policy change: INFRA-4567 is already scoped; we can land the config change in staging by next Tue (2026-12-07). Needs one more PR review.
- Canary routing: we have a template for canary routing rules but it requires a small change in the traffic router to support variant-level fallback; estimate ~3 engineer-days. I can reprioritize two engineers from the batching work to make this sprint.
- Audit logs/permissions: security will need us to provide the demo account list and a short threat summary. I can draft the request, but will need the NimbusCloud contact and a timeline.

Attachments: deployment-runbook-v1.md (stubbed run sequence + rollback).

Blockers / asks from my side:
- If we trim the reranker, confirm if we still need the extra replication capacity scheduled for week of 12/13. If yes, we need to keep commit.
- Please add a single test account for partners (NimbusCloud) to the runbook so security can approve quickly.

Will mark which tickets I will escalate if we need exec help.

-Vanessa

--
Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Cloud Partnerships & Delivery
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Sarah Park <sarah@nimbleai.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T12:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter steering: strategy trim, rapid deps & QBR artifacts

Thanks — tagging in engineering constraints.

High-level: a reduced scope is preferable; it gives us runway to stabilize routing and caching which are higher ROI for the quarter. Specifics:

- Latency SLOs: removing the full quantization rollout should not materially change our p95 if we invest the saved cycles into the routing optimization I'm proposing (continuous batching adjustments + kernel tuning). I can commit an initial tuning pass by 12/10 if we move the reranker off the critical path.
- Replication capacity: if we trim reranker replication we can avoid the extra nodes for the demo. That saves approx $6k/month and reduces ops surface.

I will: 
- Open a short-lived spike branch for the canary fallback change and assign to Alex + Priya.
- Add the infra tickets to JIRA and link INFRA-4567.

Related links: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/eng/runbooks/canary-fallback-design and JIRA:INFRA-4567.

Small ask for leadership: if security needs faster turnaround on audit evidence, we may need an exception for 48-hour expedited review for the demo account (one-off). Can we approve that if requested?

-Markus

--
Markus Klein
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter steering: strategy trim, rapid deps & QBR artifacts

All — good direction. I approve the proposed reduced scope and the ask list to NimbusCloud.

Two quick notes for the communication to partners: 
- Be explicit that the demo will showcase hosted->dedicated failover (not full feature parity). Set expectations.
- Provide the partner account list and demo window options (Dec 13-17 or Jan 5-9). Security will prioritize based on the chosen window.

On expedited review: I approve a single 48-hour exception for the audit evidence if infrastructure flags it as blocking. Vanessa, please prepare a short escalation note and I'll sign off.

Naomi

--
Naomi Feldman
VP, Customer Success & GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
